mappings.note: Naming the substances derived from petroleum and gas as petrochemicals identifies materials by origin. Not LO-27, because no use is named.
Petroleum as black gold identifies a material from a familiar name. Duplicate of an earlier item and coded the same way.
Coal tar going into naphthalene balls is an everyday application of a by-product. Not LO-20, which covers how the by-product is made rather than what it becomes.
What petrochemicals are used to manufacture is an application question. Not LO-16, because the item asks the use rather than the origin.
Advising a pollution-conscious driver which fuel to use is an environmental choice about resource use. Not LO-27, because the point is the cleaner option rather than the fuel's ordinary use.
Defining minerals places substances within the natural-resource scheme. Not LO-16, because a class rather than a property is at issue.
Petroleum being a mixture of hydrocarbons is material composition. Not LO-17, because no resource class is assigned.

Excluding the substance that is not a coal product rests on knowing what destructive distillation yields, a process. Not LO-16, because the answer depends on the processing rather than on composition.
Picking the petrochemical identifies a material by its origin in petroleum. Not LO-17, whose classification is of resources as exhaustible or inexhaustible.
Carbonisation as the conversion of dead vegetation is a process explanation. Grouped with the other formation items.
The full form of LPG identifies a material by what it is. Not LO-27, since no use is asked for.
Natural gas under high pressure being CNG names a material by its state. Not LO-20, because compressing is not the process being explained here.
Bitumen for road surfacing is an application of a petroleum product. Grouped with the other use items.
The products of destructive distillation are the outputs of a process, which LO-20 covers. Not LO-21, because these are not reactions with air, water or acid.
Naming undersea oil extraction describes how the resource is obtained, a process. Not LO-27, because nothing is applied in daily life.
Butane as the main constituent of LPG is composition. Duplicate in substance of the earlier LPG item.
Bitumen for road surfacing is an application of a petroleum product. Duplicate of the item above and coded the same way.
The least polluting vehicle fuel is an environmental choice. Grouped with the other clean-fuel items rather than with the classification ones.
Where petroleum is found is part of explaining how and where the resource forms. Not LO-17, because no class is assigned.
Which Indian region has no natural gas field is knowledge of where the resource occurs. Grouped with the occurrence and formation items on LO-20.
Matching coal, petroleum and methane to solid, liquid and gas differentiates materials by physical state. Not LO-17, because states rather than resource classes are compared.
The petroleum fraction used in paints and road surfacing is an application question. Grouped with the other use items.
The conversion of buried vegetation into coal under heat and pressure is the carbonisation process. Duplicate in substance of the earlier carbonisation items.
Filling in a product and its by-product from coal processing rests on the destructive distillation process. Not LO-16, because outputs of a process rather than composition are tested.
Excluding the substance not obtained from petroleum rests on what refining yields. Grouped with the coal-product item for the same reason.
Identifying petroleum from colour, smell and the range of products it yields is identification by properties. Not LO-17, because the resource class is already given in the stem.
What carbonisation is names a process. Duplicate in substance of the other carbonisation items.
Completing the sentence about dead vegetation turning slowly into coal is the same process explanation. Coded with its duplicates.

Weighing three statements about what fossil fuels are and what overuse does is a test of the resource class itself. LO-28 was rejected because the item judges statements rather than asking for a protective measure.
Picking the exhaustible resource is LO-17's own example. Not LO-28, because nothing is conserved.
Choosing the correct statement about fossil fuels tests the defining facts of that resource class. Not LO-20, because no process is explained.
What the Petroleum Conservation Research Association discourages is about using a resource judiciously. Not LO-27, because the item is about conservation rather than use.
Picking out a natural resource is classification within the resource scheme. Not LO-16, because no property is compared.
Naming inexhaustible resources is the classification LO-17 states verbatim. Grouped with the other resource items.
Calling limited resources exhaustible is the same classification from the other side. Coded with its counterparts.
Picking the exhaustible natural resource is the classification outcome. Duplicate in substance of an earlier item.
Sunlight placed among inexhaustible resources is resource classification. Not LO-28, because nothing is being conserved.
Petroleum placed among exhaustible resources is the same classification applied to a fossil fuel. Coded with the sunlight item as its opposite case.
Carbonisation as the slow conversion of dead vegetation is a process explanation. Duplicate of an earlier item and coded the same way.
The gas from burning coal in plentiful air is a combustion product, the substance of the word-equation outcome. Duplicate of an earlier item.
